desc:
Android integrations connect your app to the services behind your business: billing, analytics, push messages and your own backend. Ecom Swift LLC wires each one into your app and tests it with your own accounts and keys.

## What are Android integrations?

An integration is the code and configuration that lets your app exchange data with another service. Examples include Play Billing for purchases, Firebase for analytics and push, an email tool for sign-ups, and a REST API that holds your customer records.

Done well, the user never notices. Done badly, purchases fail, events go missing and data does not match what the server holds.

## Why integrations deserve careful work

Most apps stop being useful when they sit alone. A store app needs orders to reach the server. A subscription app needs to know which users have paid. A support tool needs to receive messages. Each of these depends on keys, permissions, request formats and error handling that must all agree.

Mistakes cost real money and trust. A purchase that is charged but not unlocked produces angry users. A broken analytics event hides the numbers you rely on. A key placed carelessly in the app can be copied by others. Care at the start avoids those problems.

## How integrations affect revenue and operations

Billing decides whether you can charge at all, and restoring purchases decides whether paying users keep access on a new phone. Analytics tells you which screens people use and where they leave. Push messages bring people back at the right time. Backend sync keeps the app and your website in step, which saves your team from manual data entry.

Each connection also reduces support questions, because the app behaves the way the user expects. The effect on revenue depends on your product and audience, and no integration produces sales by itself. It makes the machinery work.

## What a well-built integration includes

- A reading of the provider's current documentation before any code is written.
- Keys and credentials created inside your own accounts, never ours.
- Code placed in its own module, so it can be changed without touching unrelated screens.
- Clear handling of failed requests, timeouts and expired sessions.
- Retry and offline behavior, so actions are not lost on a weak connection.
- Sandbox or test mode checks for every service before real data is used.
- Analytics events named consistently on the actions you choose.
- Secrets kept out of the app code where the provider allows it.
- A restore purchases flow when billing is included.
- Plain setup notes that explain how each piece is configured.

## How we work

We list the services you want and confirm what each must do. Then we connect them one at a time and test each against its sandbox. The Basic package connects one service with error handling. Standard connects up to three, adds analytics events, backend calls and offline handling. Premium covers a complete set including Play Billing, Firebase Cloud Messaging push, backend sync and crash monitoring.

When a card payment on Android is needed, the platform's own billing rules apply to digital goods, and we explain which route fits your product before building.

## Checklist for safe integrations

**Do:**
- Create the provider accounts in your own name before we start.
- Send API documentation or sample requests for your backend.
- Decide which events you want to measure.
- Test with a small group before releasing to everyone.
- Keep the setup notes with your project files.

**Avoid:**
- Sharing provider logins in chat or email.
- Putting secret keys directly in app code that ships to phones.
- Connecting services you have no plan to use.
- Assuming sandbox success equals live success without a final check.
- Leaving error messages vague, so users cannot tell what failed.

## Who this is for

A subscription app owner who needs billing and entitlement checks to agree. A retailer who wants the app to read products and send orders to an existing backend. A startup that needs analytics and push before inviting its first testers. A developer who knows the app well but lacks time to learn another provider's setup.

## What we need from you

List the services, send any backend documentation and tell us who owns each account. We ask you to invite us with limited roles instead of sharing logins, and we never need your passwords. If your backend lacks documentation, we can work from sample responses and tell you what we find.
